content: WASF1, also referred to as Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein family member 1 or WAVE1, is a protein encoded by the WASF1 gene in humans. This protein belongs to the Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein (WASP) family and plays a pivotal role in cellular processes regulated by Rac, a small GTPase of the Rho family. Specifically, WASF1 is a key component of the WAVE regulatory complex, which is essential for the regulation of the actin cytoskeleton. This regulation is critical for processes such as membrane ruffling, a dynamic cellular activity involved in cell motility and signaling. The WASF1 protein has been demonstrated to associate with the Arp2/3 complex, a core actin nucleation factor. Through this interaction, WASF1 enhances actin polymerization in vitro, thereby contributing to the reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton. Clinically, Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is an immunodeficiency disorder that is thought to arise from defects in the regulation of the actin cytoskeleton. This highlights the importance of proteins like WASF1 in maintaining proper immune system function. In terms of molecular interactions, WASF1 has been shown to interact with BAIAP2 (Brain-specific angiogenesis inhibitor 1-associated protein 2) and Profilin 1, both of which are involved in actin dynamics and cytoskeletal regulation.
